chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah ibn Muhammad al-Ghifari from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever honors his Muslim brother with a word that softens him and relieves his distress, will remain in the extended shade of Allah and mercy as long as he continues doing so.'

key_terms.یُلْطِفُهُ: he softens him / treats him gently

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for honoring a Muslim brother with kind words?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-A'mal*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) to emphasize the spiritual weight of verbal comfort, linking it to the concept of *Zill Allah* (Allah's Shade) during the Day of Judgment. This tradition underscores the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) in social interactions, where alleviating a brother's distress through gentle speech is not merely a social courtesy but a direct path to divine proximity and sustained mercy.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam  Ja’far  Sadiq  (a.s.)  narrates  that  the  Holy  Prophet (s.a.w.s.)   said,   “One   who   respects   a   Muslim   while conversing,  Allah  will  love  him  and  solve  his  difficulties. That person will remain in Allah’s mercy till he continues doing so.”
